statement:
Let \(P(x) = x^4 - x^3 + x\).\\
a) Prove that for all positive real numbers \(a\), the polynomial \(P(x) - a\) has a unique positive zero.\\
b) A sequence \((a_n)\) is defined by \(a_1 = \tfrac{1}{3}\) and for all \(n \geq 1\), \(a_{n+1}\) is the positive zero of \(P(x) - a_n\). Prove that \((a_n)\) converges and find its limit.

For each non-negative integer \(n\), let \(u_n = (2+\sqrt{5})^n + (2-\sqrt{5})^n\).\\
a) Prove that \(u_n\) is a positive integer for all \(n \geq 0\). What is the largest possible remainder when \(u_n\) is divided by \(24\)?\\
b) Find all pairs of positive integers \((a,b)\) with \(a, b < 500\) such that for all odd positive integers \(n\), \(u_n \equiv a^n - b^n \pmod{1111}\).

Let \(ABC\) be an acute scalene triangle with circumcenter \(O\), circumcircle \((O)\), orthocenter \(H\). Line \(AH\) meets \((O)\) again at \(D 
eq A\). Let \(E, F\) be the midpoints of \(AB, AC\). The line through \(H\) perpendicular to \(HF\) meets \(BC\) at \(K\).\
a) Line \(DK\) meets \((O)\) again at \(Y 
eq D\). Prove that the intersection of line \(BY\) and the perpendicular bisector of \(BK\) lies on the circumcircle of \(	riangle OFY\).\
b) The line through \(H\) perpendicular to \(HE\) meets \(BC\) at \(L\). Line \(DL\) meets \((O)\) again at \(Z 
eq D\). Let \(M\) = \(BZ \cap OE\), \(N\) = \(CY \cap OF\), \(P\) = \(BY \cap CZ\). Let \(T\) = \(YZ \cap MN\) and \(d\) the line through \(T\) perpendicular to \(OA\). Prove that \(d\) bisects \(AP\).

Let \(ABC\) be an acute scalene triangle with altitudes \(AD, BE, CF\) where \(D \in BC\), \(E \in CA\), \(F \in AB\). Let \(H, O, I\) be the orthocenter, circumcenter, incenter and \(M, N, P\) the midpoints of \(BC, CA, AB\). Let \(X, Y, Z\) be the intersections of \((AI, NP)\), \((BI, PM)\), \((CI, MN)\) respectively.\\
a) Prove that the circumcircles of \(\triangle AXD\), \(\triangle BYE\), \(\triangle CZF\) have two common points lying on line \(OH\).\\
b) Lines \(XP, YM, ZN\) meet the circumcircles of \(\triangle AXD, \triangle BYE, \triangle CZF\) again at \(X', Y', Z'\). Let \(J\) be the reflection of \(I\) across \(O\). Prove that \(X', Y', Z'\) lie on a line perpendicular to \(HJ\).

Consider a \(3k \times 3k\) grid (\(k\) a positive integer). Place \(4k\) marbles with at most one per cell such that every row and column has at least one marble, and every marble shares its row or column with at least one other marble.\\
a) For \(k = 1\), determine the number of valid placements.\\
b) For \(k \geq 1\), find the largest positive integer \(N\) such that for any \(N\) marked cells, there exists a valid placement of \(4k\) marbles with none on marked cells.

Let \(a, b, c\) be non-negative numbers with \(a + b + c = 3\). Prove that
\[\sqrt{3a^3+4bc+b+c}+\sqrt{3b^3+4ca+c+a}+\sqrt{3c^3+4ab+a+b} \geq 9.\]
